    def dfun(self, state_variables, coupling, local_coupling=0):

        # shape (n_sv, n_modes)
        V_e = state_variables[0, :]

        r_e = state_variables[2, :]

        Delta_e = self.Delta_e
        Delta_i = self.Delta_i
        Gamma = self.Gamma
        I_e = self.I_e
        I_i = self.I_i

        tau_i = self.tau_i
        tau_s = self.tau_s

        # Coupling Terms (from coupling array)
        c_glob = coupling[0, :]

        # Derived Variables

        # Time Derivatives
        # Broadcast every derivative to a common per-node shape so constant
        # (state-independent) derivatives — e.g. ``duA/dt = cA`` — stack into a
        # homogeneous array alongside node-shaped ones, matching TVB's own
        # ``numpy.full_like`` handling of constant drifts.

            np.asarray(
                (
                    I_e
                    + eta_e
                    + V_e**2
                    + s_ee * tau_e
                    - s_ei * tau_e
                    - np.pi**2 * r_e**2 * tau_e**2
                )
                / tau_e
            ),  # V_e
            np.asarray(
                (
                    I_i
                    + eta_i
                    + V_i**2
                    + s_ie * tau_i
                    - s_ii * tau_i
                    - np.pi**2 * r_i**2 * tau_i**2
                )
                / tau_i
            ),  # V_i

            np.asarray((2 * V_i * r_i + Delta_i / (np.pi * tau_i)) / tau_i),  # r_i
            np.asarray((c_glob - s_ee + J_ee * r_e) / tau_s),  # s_ee
            np.asarray((-s_ei + J_ei * r_i) / tau_s),  # s_ei
            np.asarray((-s_ie + Gamma * c_glob + J_ie * r_e) / tau_s),  # s_ie
            np.asarray((-s_ii + J_ii * r_i) / tau_s),  # s_ii
        )
        return np.array(_derivs)
